frames.narration: Twelve call sites need data from deep inside an order: tax rate, country, street. Each one walks the chain order, customer, address, country by itself.
A change arrives: customers get several addresses, and the old address becomes the billing one. Tax should follow the shipping address.

Nine call sites crossed that link, in 7 different modules. They still compile and still run, and they now charge tax by the billing country: 190 where 200 is right. Every one must be found and edited.
Tell, don't ask: the sites call order.tax() and the rule lives in the classes that hold the data. The same change is now 4 one-line edits in one class, Customer, and no call site changes.

Now the over-applied extreme: give every class a forwarding method for every piece of data behind it. The chains are gone, but the order exposes 8 methods and the classes together hold 18 that only forward.

The sites still ask for the tax rate and decide what to do with it, so a rule change such as a reduced rate under 50.00 must still be made in 2 places. Adding a currency field at the far end needs a hop in every class on the way: 5 edits, against 1 for a train wreck.

Over four changes in the model: train-wreck calls need 18 edits in 16 places, tell needs 14 edits in 8, forwarding everything needs 17 edits in 9. Tell helps most where behaviour changes, and costs a little more where a new field is added.
